source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master item says complete Storage inventory, but its Procedure and command read one PCIe member. These differ in resource family and population. DeepSeek's Storage command is a third-party correction attempt, not authority, so it cannot resolve the preserved Master contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Purpose and target identity remain irreducibly ambiguous: choosing Storage would discard the authoritative PCIe Procedure, while choosing PCIe cannot satisfy all-connected Storage inventory. An owner source correction is required before any execution contract exists.

review_improvement: Prevents a successful wrong-resource GET from being reported as full storage inventory and defines the exact owner decision needed to unblock the row.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PCIe member response proves only one object in a PCIe graph; a Storage collection response proves only the top-level Storage graph and still requires member/Drive traversal for all connected devices. Because the Master ties the Storage title to the PCIe path, there is no evidence-based way to decide whether the copy error is in the title, path or both. Running the more plausible DeepSeek command would silently rewrite the test, so no command is authorized until the owner fixes identity and completeness semantics.
